items.title: Keycloak has authentication bypass via jwt algorithm confusion
items.summary: ### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak. This JWT algorithm confusion vulnerability in the JWT Authorization Grant flow allows an attacker with valid client credentials to bypass signature verification. By forging an assertion, the attacker can create unauthorized access tokens. This enables the attacker to impersonate any federated user linked to the affected Identity Provider, leading to unauthorized access and potential privilege escalation.

items.title: SD JWT JS: Tampered disclosures silently dropped instead of rejected
items.summary: ## Summary  When one Disclosure in an SD-JWT presentation is tampered so its digest no longer matches the Issuer-signed `_sd` array, `@sd-jwt/decode` 0.19.0 does **not** reject the presentation. It silently drops the unmatched Disclosure and returns a **reduced claim set**, reporting success. The Issuer signature is untouched and valid.  This is a downgrade/omission primitive. A malicious or curious **holder** can present a tampered Disclosure and have the relying party receive *fewer* claims than the credential carries, with no error surfaced.

items.title: AdminNeo: CSRF Token Secret Recoverable from Single Observed Token, Enabling Cross-Site Request Forgery

items.title: joi: quadratic-time split in `string().email({ multiple: true })` allows denial of service
items.summary: ### Summary  `Joi.string().email({ multiple: true })` takes quadratic time to split a value that contains a long run of whitespace. One request with 100 KB of spaces blocks the Node.js event loop for several seconds, which causes a denial of service.  ### Details  When the `multiple` option is set, the `email` rule splits the value into addresses with a regular expression that removes whitespace on each side of the separator:  ```js const regex = new RegExp(`\\s*[${options.separator ? escapeRegex(options.separator) : ','}]\\s*`); // ... const e

items.title: Forge: verifyCertificateChain() removes trusted CA certificates with the same subject from the CA store
items.summary: ### Summary  When a CA store created by `pki.createCaStore()` holds two or more certificates with the same subject name, `pki.verifyCertificateChain()` permanently removes those certificates from the store while trying each one as the issuer. A peer can send any certificate that names that subject as its issuer to make all later verifications against those CA certificates fail. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.  ### Details  `pki.verifyCertificateChain()` (`lib/x509.js`) asks the CA store for the issuer of each certificate with `caStore.getIssuer()`.

items.title: pypdf has possible long runtimes when retrieving page labels
items.summary: ### Impact  An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large runtimes. This requires retrieving the page labels of a file.  ### Patches  This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.3](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.3).  ### Workarounds  If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4251](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4251).

items.title: Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal
items.summary: ### Summary  In glob 13.0.6, an aborted async walk rejects or emits an error but continues recursively reading directories in the background.  The root cause is that abort branches in src/walker.ts call cb() without returning. As a result, callers that rely on signal or AbortSignal.timeout() to bound glob traversal cost can still incur filesystem I/O and CPU work after the request has already been rejected.  ### Details  This was reproduced on glob v13.0.6 (commit e80cb38ae60d6cbff9e75f39032a994858994d35). items.title: pyasn1 has quadratic CPU consumption in constructed BIT STRING decoding
items.summary: ## Summary  In pyasn1 through 0.6.4, decoding a constructed BIT STRING with many fragments repeatedly shifts and copies the entire value accumulated so far. For fixed-size fragments, CPU time grows quadratically with the encoded input size. An application that passes sufficiently large, attacker-controlled ASN.1 data to an affected decoder can suffer CPU exhaustion during `decode()`; no conversion or formatting of the decoded value is required. items.title: Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted HTTP/2 Server via Rapid Stream Reset
items.summary: ## Summary  An uncontrolled-resource-consumption vulnerability (CWE-400) in the Twisted HTTP/2 server lets any unauthenticated remote client exhaust server CPU over a single connection. A client that sends a request header block with `END_STREAM` and then immediately resets the stream makes the server route and render the request before it processes the reset. items.title: zip: Arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory, because ZipArchive::extract validates symlink targets lexically.
items.summary: ### Summary  - **Verified version:** zip `9.0.0-pre3` - **Affected versions:** `7.2.0` and later - **Precondition:** The attacker knows (or can guess) the absolute path of the extraction destination  The validation applied to symlinks is purely lexical. As a result, an attacker can write arbitrary files outside the extraction directory through a symlink. Exploitation requires the attacker to know (or guess) the absolute path of the destination, but this is realistic in practice: CI workspaces, `/opt/app`, a fixed Downloads path, and so on.  > *

items.title: Keycloak vulnerable to information disclosure through arbitrary filesystem path probing
items.summary: ### Description A flaw was found in Keycloak. A realm administrator with the "manage-realm" role can exploit this vulnerability by submitting an arbitrary filesystem path as a keystore parameter when creating a key provider component. This allows the administrator to probe arbitrary filesystem paths, determining which files exist and are readable by the Keycloak process. This information disclosure could be used to identify high-value targets for follow-on attacks.

items.title: Shopify App: Token exchange shop context confusion may allow cross-shop authorization bypass in affected apps
items.summary: In token-exchange authenticated controllers, `shopify_app` exposes shop context through helpers such as `current_shopify_domain`. Prior to the fix, `current_shopify_domain` could resolve to the sanitized `shop` query parameter instead of the shop identity derived from the verified Shopify ID token or active Shopify session.
